sentences.text: The inventory record covers serviceable parts, consumables, repairable units, and their locations across shore and offshore stores.
Warehouse System maintains the authoritative item catalogue, stock balances, and storage locations.
Stock visibility includes quantities on hand, items reserved for approved work, and quantities already committed to transfer.
Spares Hub provides a separate view of stock held for regional replenishment and emergency support.
The Storekeeper reconciles physical counts with recorded balances and records adjustments with a reason and timestamp.
Each stocked item is identified by a controlled part number, description, unit of measure, and approved substitute status.
Serial-controlled parts retain traceability from receipt through installation, repair, return, or disposal.
Reservations prevent the same available quantity from being assigned to multiple work packages.
Maintenance Planning Engine uses planned work demand and part criticality to support replenishment forecasts.
The Duty Planner reviews forecast demand against current stock before confirming work readiness.
Priority is highest for safety-critical parts and parts required to restore a turbine or electrical system to service.
Parts supporting scheduled maintenance receive priority when their delivery date is necessary to protect an approved work window.
Routine consumables are replenished according to agreed minimum and maximum stock levels.
Replenishment requests include the required quantity, need date, delivery location, and applicable handling requirements.
Supplier lead times are reviewed against recent delivery performance rather than relying solely on catalogue estimates.
Low-stock alerts identify items approaching their reorder point and show open purchase commitments.
A shortage that threatens a work window is escalated to the Duty Planner for a priority decision.
The Storekeeper records unavailable quantities and the expected date of the next supply without presenting them as available stock.
Substitutions require engineering acceptance and confirmation that the alternative meets the required interface and operating limits.
Damaged, suspect, or expired parts are segregated from usable stock until their status is resolved.
A count discrepancy is investigated against receipts, issues, reservations, and recent movements before the balance is corrected.
Urgent purchases require documented authorization and retain the same traceability and inspection controls as routine receipts.
During transport, the dispatch record identifies the quantity, destination, handling conditions, and responsible receiving location.
Returned parts are inspected and their condition is recorded before they are restored to available stock.
Repeated delays, shortages, and count discrepancies are reviewed to adjust reorder levels and supplier priorities.
